title: Relative Cech spectral sequence for small-etale structure-sheaf modules
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $u:U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale morphism from a scheme. Form $U_p=U\times_X\cdots\times_XU$ with $p+1$ factors, $p\geq0$, with augmentation $u_p:U_p\to X$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; the face maps omit a factor. Use the canonical small etale ringed topoi, their localization identifications [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and module direct images and tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $M$ be any $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^q(f\circ u_p)_*(M|_{U_p})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R^{p+q}f_*M.$$
Here $M|_{U_p}=u_p^*M$ is etale restriction, and all right derived functors are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The first differential is the alternating sum of the face restriction maps. For each $n\geq0$ the abutment has a finite decreasing filtration $R^nf_*M=F^0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}=0$ with $F^p/F^{p+1}\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$, and each entry stabilizes to $E_\infty^{p,q}$ for sufficiently large page. No quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, separation, flatness of $f$, or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 072E, lemma-cech-to-cohomology-relative-modules and its double-complex proof; small-etale localization version, as suggested in spaces-cohomology.tex immediately before Tag 0720 (lemma-higher-direct-image). proof.text: Pass to the enlarged etale ringed sites $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$. The equivalences with the small etale module categories preserve injectives and exact sequences: an equivalence and its inverse preserve kernels, cokernels and the extension property defining injectivity. For an etale scheme $V\to Y$ put $W=X\times_YV$ and $W_p=U_p\times_YV$. Etale permanence gives all $u_p$ and face maps etale. Base change of the atlas is the singleton covering $W_0\to W$ in $\mathcal C_X$, and $W_p=W_0\times_W\cdots\times_WW_0$. The fibre-product lemma gives these objects and covering stability; representability of $u$ makes each $U_p$ a scheme. The enlarged-site model identifies each $\mathcal C_{U_p}$ with $\mathcal C_X/U_p$ and its structure sheaf with the restricted ring. The chart-limit identification identifies the specified module direct images with the enlarged ringed direct images, including their restrictions and scalar actions. Thus all subsequent computations compute the functors in the statement, rather than a different choice of direct image.

The specified module direct images are additive right adjoints: their adjunctions identify maps into the direct image of a kernel with maps killed by the corresponding image morphism, proving preservation of kernels; linearity gives additivity. The module category on $\mathcal C_X$ is Grothendieck abelian by the arbitrary-ring-sheaf theorem, hence has enough injectives. Choose a resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$ by the nonnegative-resolution existence lemma. For every $p$, the localization functor $u_p^*$ is exact and has an exact additive left adjoint $u_{p!}$ by the ringed-slice adjunction. Apply the exact-left-adjoint criterion to $u_{p!}\dashv u_p^*$: every $u_p^*I^q$ is injective. Exactness of $u_p^*$ preserves the augmented exact resolution, so $u_p^*I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of $u_p^*M$. This argument uses the localization $u_p$, and imposes no exactness assumption on tensor pullback along $f$.

proof.text: Set $B^{p,q}=(fu_p)_*(u_p^*I^q)$ for $p,q\geq0$. Define $d_h=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^i\delta_i^*$ by face restrictions and $d_v=(fu_p)_*u_p^*(d_I)$. On a test $V\to Y$, the chart-limit identification gives $B^{p,q}(V)=\widetilde I^q(W_p)$, with face maps the actual restrictions along the projections $W_{p+1}\to W_p$. Every restriction is $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear because both scalar actions are pulled back from $V$, and the identifications commute with maps of tests. The identities between two factor-deletion maps cancel the terms of $d_h^2$ in pairs. Naturality of $d_I$ under restriction gives $d_hd_v=d_vd_h$, and $d_v^2=0$. These equations on tests give a first-quadrant double complex of module sheaves. Use its finite-diagonal total complex with differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$.

source.place: Tag 072E (lemma-cech-to-cohomology-relative-modules), double-complex construction; homology.tex section-double-complex and definition-associated-simple-complex.

proof.text:
Fix $q$ and an etale scheme $V\to Y$. Apply injective-module Cech acyclicity to the injective $\widetilde I^q$ on $\mathcal C_X$ and the singleton covering $W_0\to W$. The chosen small-site convention allows the site objects, module values, ring values and singleton covering index to be placed in one common larger universe, as required by that node. The positive cohomology of $\widetilde I^q(W_\bullet)$ vanishes. In degree zero the sheaf equalizer axiom identifies its kernel with $\widetilde I^q(W)$, by restriction along $W_0\to W$. The chart-limit identification therefore makes
$$0\longrightarrow (f_*I^q)(V)\longrightarrow B^{0,q}(V)\longrightarrow B^{1,q}(V)\longrightarrow\cdots$$
exact for every $V$. This is exactness as $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-modules since all arrows are linear. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels, so this sectionwise exact augmented complex is exact as module sheaves. In particular $f_*I^q\simeq\ker(d_h:B^{0,q}\to B^{1,q})$.

source.place: Tag 03FC (lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech); stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 072E, augmented injective-row calculation.

proof.text:
The restriction maps $a^q:f_*I^q\to B^{0,q}$ commute with $d_I$, and $d_ha^q=0$ by the equalizer calculation. Hence $b:f_*I^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}B$, whose component is $a^q$ followed by inclusion in bidegree $(0,q)$, is a chain map: on that summand the vertical total sign is $+1$, and the horizontal term vanishes. For every fixed $q$, Step 4 says exactly that the map from $f_*I^q$ in horizontal degree zero to the row $B^{\bullet,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the first-quadrant column-augmentation lemma with $K=B$ and $A=f_*I^\bullet$ (its hypothesis is on the columns of $K.\mathrm{flip}$). It proves that this specified $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus
$$H^n(\operatorname{Tot}B)\simeq H^n(f_*I^\bullet)=R^nf_*M,$$
where the last equality is the definition of right derived functors on injective resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), second-variable variant; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 072E, total augmentation.

proof.text:
Apply the first spectral sequence of the first-quadrant double-complex theorem to $B$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Its first page is $H^q(B^{p,\bullet})$. By Step 2 and the definition of right derived functors this equals $R^q(fu_p)_*(u_p^*M)$, and the theorem identifies $d_1$ with the map on vertical cohomology induced by $d_h$, namely the alternating sum of face restriction maps. Its abutment is the object identified in Step 5. Transport the theorem's image filtration on total cohomology across that identification to obtain
$$R^nf_*M=F^0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}=0,\qquad F^p/F^{p+1}\simeq E_\infty^{p,n-p}.$$
The same theorem gives entrywise stabilization (in particular for $r>\max(p,q+1)$). Only $0\leq p\leq n$ occur in total degree $n$, so these assertions require no finiteness of the atlas or geometric finiteness condition on $f$.

For a module morphism $h:M\to N$, choose nonnegative injective resolutions $I,J$. The resolution-lift lemma gives $t:I\to J$ over $h$. Restriction and direct image give a double-complex map $B(t)$, hence spectral-sequence maps and a compatible filtered abutment map by functoriality of the double-complex theorem. Any two lifts are homotopic by the uniqueness-up-to-homotopy theorem, applied to $M[0]\to I$ and the bounded-below injective target $J$. If $s$ is such a homotopy, its image in each fixed column is a vertical homotopy, so the two maps agree on $E_1$: their difference on a vertical cycle is a vertical boundary. On total complexes the signed homotopy in bidegree $(p,q)$ is $(-1)^p(fu_p)_*u_p^*(s^q)$. Substitution in $dH+Hd$ cancels the horizontal cross terms and gives the difference of the two total maps. It preserves the first filtration, and therefore satisfies the filtration-shift hypothesis of the filtered-homotopy theorem; this gives agreement on all later pages and on the filtered abutment. The augmentation commutes with $t$ by naturality of restriction. Apply this construction to the identity between any two resolutions; the reverse comparison and the uniqueness result give inverse page and filtered-abutment isomorphisms. Identity and composition follow by comparing the composite lifts. Thus the spectral sequence is natural in $M$ and independent of the resolution from $E_1$ onwards.
